messages.subject: looping through stat_function fails
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to adde a series of stat_function curves using a loop, but when I run the loop, only one of the curves is printed out. See below for code.

frame2 = data.frame(height=height+ runif(N,-.2,.2),earn=(earnings))

m2 <- ggplot(frame2,aes(x=height,y=earn))
m2 <- m2 + geom_point() + scale_y_continuous("Earnings",limits=c(-1000,200000)) + scale_x_continuous("Height") + theme_bw()
for (i in 1:20)
  m2 <- m2 + stat_function(aes(y=0),fun=function(x) exp(fit1.post$beta[4000-i,1]+fit1.post$beta[4000-i,2]*x),colour="grey")
m2 + stat_function(fun=function(x) exp(beta.mean[1] + beta.mean[2]*x),colour="red")



Thanks,
Peter

messages.author: 4e979d95e92a2b9e
messages.subject: Re: looping through stat_function fails
parts:
Peter--

My best guess, from the way your code is formatted in the email, is that you need curly braces to define what happens for (i in 1:20):

for (i in 1:20) {
  m2 <- m2 + stat_function(aes(y=0),
                                fun=function(x) exp(fit1.post$beta[4000-i,1]+fit1.post$beta[4000-i,2]*x),
                                colour="grey")
}

Other than that, you don't give a reproducible example, or even state which curve is plotted, so folks can't be of too much help.

You can easily test if the issue is in your looping or in your ggplot2 code by copying and pasting the line interspersed with explicitly setting i:
i <- 1
  m2 <- m2 + stat_function(aes(y=0),
                                fun=function(x) exp(fit1.post$beta[4000-i,1]+fit1.post$beta[4000-i,2]*x),
                                colour="grey")
plot(m2)
i <- 2
  m2 <- m2 + stat_function(aes(y=0),
                                fun=function(x) exp(fit1.post$beta[4000-i,1]+fit1.post$beta[4000-i,2]*x),
                                colour="grey")
plot(m2)
etc.

I hope that this helps.  If not, please provide the list with a bit more information on what is happening, so we have something to work with.

Tom

Still ain't reproducible. Took me 5 min just to install Stan and then you didn't include earnings_one_pred.sm.RData. 

Still, I wanted to see if I could do it and this is what I came up with. It ain't elegant, but it's pretty cool to watch it draw. 

df<-data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10)

a<-"ggplot(data=df, aes(x=x, y=y))+\n geom_point()+\n"
for (i in 1:10){
if (i < 10){
a<- paste(a, "stat_function(fun=function(x) ",  i, "*x ,colour=`grey`)+\n")
}
if (i == 10){
a<- paste(a, "stat_function(fun=function(x) ", i, "*x ,colour=`grey`)")
}
}

eval(parse(text = a))

HTH, 
B

Dear Ggplot Community,

I have a similar problem as explained in the thread below.
I would like to plot several interaction effects across groups, based on regression coefficients and intercepts that I get from previous analysis. I can plot it by default. However, I want to generalize the script via a function and that doesn't really seem to work.
Could you maybe help me figure out where I am going wrong? Or which loophole I am not aware of?


Here's a (hopefully) reproducible snippet. My aim is to get identical graphs for concrete.graph and gen.graph.

Thanks a lot for your input!


##'Defining the objects
rm<-data.frame(x=1:5,1000,replace=T)
rm$y<-rm$x*4+4
beta.df<-data.frame(group=c(1,2,3), intercept=c(0.35,0.37,0.5),m3=c(0.2,0.35,0.3)) 
col<-c("red","blue","green")


#Effects for 3 groups
poly1r <- function(x) {beta.df$intercept[1]+beta.df$m3[1]*x}
poly2r <- function(x) {beta.df$intercept[2]+beta.df$m3[2]*x}
poly3r <- function(x) {beta.df$intercept[3]+beta.df$m3[3]*x}


concrete.graph<-ggplot(rm,aes(x=x))
concrete.graph<-concrete.graph+stat_function(fun = poly1r, colour="black", size=2)
concrete.graph<-concrete.graph+stat_function(fun = poly2r, colour="red", size=2)
concrete.graph<-concrete.graph+stat_function(fun = poly3r, colour="blue", size=2)
concrete.graph


###Generalized function (for n groups)
mini.graph<- function (n) {
graph<-ggplot(relmo,aes(x=rel))
for (g in 1:n) {
polyr <- function(x) {beta.df$intercept[g]+beta.df$m3[g]*x}
graph<-graph+stat_function(fun = polyr, colour=col[g], size=2)
}
return(graph)
}

gen.graph<-mini.graph(3)

Hello,

just a small follow up.
Thanks to Brandon's example, I finally managed to make it work!

mini.graph<- function (n) {
a<-"ggplot(data=rm,aes(x=x))+\n"
for (i in 1:n){
if (i < n){
a<- paste(a, "stat_function(fun=function(x) ",  beta.df$intercept[i],"+",beta.df$m3[i],"*x ,colour=\"",col[i],"\") +\n")
}
if (i == n){
a<- paste(a, "stat_function(fun=function(x) ", beta.df$intercept[i],"+",beta.df$m3[i],"*x ,colour=\"",col[i],"\")")

}
}
gr<-eval(parse(text = a))
return(gr)
}

g<-mini.graph(3)

On Thursday, March 13, 2014 6:56:14 PM UTC+1, ignacz...@gmail.com wrote:
Dear Ggplot Community,

I have a similar problem as explained in the thread below.
I would like to plot several interaction effects across groups, based on regression coefficients and intercepts that I get from previous analysis. I can plot it by default. However, I want to generalize the script via a function and that doesn't really seem to work.
Could you maybe help me figure out where I am going wrong? Or which loophole I am not aware of?


Here's a (hopefully) reproducible snippet. My aim is to get identical graphs for concrete.graph and gen.graph.

Thanks a lot for your input!


##'Defining the objects
rm<-data.frame(x=1:5,1000,replace=T)
rm$y<-rm$x*4+4
beta.df<-data.frame(group=c(1,2,3), intercept=c(0.35,0.37,0.5),m3=c(0.2,0.35,0.3)) 
col<-c("red","blue","green")


#Effects for 3 groups
poly1r <- function(x) {beta.df$intercept[1]+beta.df$m3[1]*x}
poly2r <- function(x) {beta.df$intercept[2]+beta.df$m3[2]*x}
poly3r <- function(x) {beta.df$intercept[3]+beta.df$m3[3]*x}


concrete.graph<-ggplot(rm,aes(x=x))
concrete.graph<-concrete.graph+stat_function(fun = poly1r, colour="black", size=2)
concrete.graph<-concrete.graph+stat_function(fun = poly2r, colour="red", size=2)
concrete.graph<-concrete.graph+stat_function(fun = poly3r, colour="blue", size=2)
concrete.graph


###Generalized function (for n groups)
mini.graph<- function (n) {
graph<-ggplot(relmo,aes(x=rel))
for (g in 1:n) {
polyr <- function(x) {beta.df$intercept[g]+beta.df$m3[g]*x}
graph<-graph+stat_function(fun = polyr, colour=col[g], size=2)
}
return(graph)
}

gen.graph<-mini.graph(3)

You mean like this?

beta.df <- data.frame(group = factor(seq(3)), intercept=c(0.35,0.37,0.5),
m3=c(0.2,0.35,0.3), cols = c("red","blue","green"))
ggplot(beta.df) +
geom_abline(aes(intercept = intercept, slope = m3, color = cols), size = 1) +
xlim(0, 5) + ylim(0, 2.5) +
labs(x = "x", y = "y") +
scale_color_identity()

Since mini.graph(3) produced the same output as above (except my lines
are deliberately thicker), you don't need a function as long as you
supply the data frame beta.df. Since the faked data in rm weren't used
in your function, I didn't use them here, but it's easy to add them
with a geom_point() layer.

Dennis

parts:
Dear Dennis,

thanks so much. You are quite write! why overcomplicate, when you can plot at once? 

it works like a charm!
cheers,
Zsofia

ps: although, oddly enough, it complains it I don't define either the xlim or ylim, I get the error: "Error in as.environment(where) : 'where' is missing". So defining the x and y axis it is.

On Tue, Mar 18, 2014 at 12:26 AM, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
You mean like this?

beta.df <- data.frame(group = factor(seq(3)), intercept=c(0.35,0.37,0.5),
                      m3=c(0.2,0.35,0.3), cols = c("red","blue","green"))
ggplot(beta.df) +
   geom_abline(aes(intercept = intercept, slope = m3, color = cols), size = 1) +
   xlim(0, 5) + ylim(0, 2.5) +
   labs(x = "x", y = "y") +
   scale_color_identity()

Since mini.graph(3) produced the same output as above (except my lines
are deliberately thicker), you don't need a function as long as you
supply the data frame beta.df. Since the faked data in rm weren't used
in your function, I didn't use them here, but it's easy to add them
with a geom_point() layer.

Dennis
